text: Embeddings are numerical vector representations of text that capture semantic meaning, allowing a computer to measure how similar two pieces of text are by comparing their vectors.
A vector database stores embeddings alongside their original content and metadata, and is optimized for fast similarity search across millions of vectors using indexes like HNSW.
Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors rather than their magnitude, making it a popular distance metric for comparing text embeddings regardless of document length.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation, or RAG, combines a retrieval step over a knowledge base with a generative language model, grounding the model's answers in retrieved documents instead of relying purely on memorized parameters.
Chunking splits long documents into smaller passages before embedding them, since embedding models have limited context windows and smaller chunks improve retrieval precision.
Prompt engineering is the practice of carefully designing input instructions to a language model to reliably produce the desired output format, tone, or reasoning process.
Fine-tuning adapts a pretrained language model to a specific task or domain by continuing training on a smaller, labeled dataset, updating some or all of the model's weights.
Git version control lets teams track changes to code over time, branch to work on features independently, and merge changes back together while preserving a full history of commits.
Writing automated unit tests with a framework like pytest helps catch bugs early by verifying that individual functions behave correctly whenever the codebase changes.
Docker packages an application together with its dependencies into a portable container image, ensuring the software runs the same way across different machines and environments.

Evaluating a language model's output quality often involves a mix of automated metrics, such as BLEU or ROUGE, and human review, since automated scores do not always capture factual correctness or helpfulness.
The transformer architecture relies on a self-attention mechanism that lets a model weigh the relevance of every other token in a sequence when producing a representation for each token.
